name: glm53_kpool_tail_slot_mapping
purpose: Keep the GLM-5.3 kpool-tail KV-cache group out of vLLM's V2 generic slot mapping (backport of vLLM #57317, upstream 70df48dc3d01), whose kernel reads that group's 32-entry block-table row by absolute position and faults once the read leaves its allocation (tessera#508).
base_image_note: The glm53_mtp_mapper derived image, the image the GLM Tessera cells name. Its MLA sparse-attention sources are stock, which Tessera's GLM53 NoPE backend requires; the MTP mapper edit is carried through unchanged.
derived_image_note: The digest is the image manifest digest the registry reports (Docker-Content-Digest, 2026-09-28). The localhost name resolves on both Sparks through docker's RepoDigests and is the name a Tessera runtime cell uses: sparky (containerd image store) reports the digest as the image Id; sparklina (overlay2) holds it as a RepoDigest over config sha256:38ead3cab558d85c2261c43dccb76207f5b25c639281cf9a24714455f14a9dc4. Both Sparks give the PrismaBuild content reference below.

build.builder_note: The classic builder, because BuildKit resolves a digest FROM against the registry over HTTPS and the LAN registry is plain HTTP. The classic builder drops a RUN heredoc's body, so the self-check is a copied file rather than a heredoc.
build.push_note: Pushed through an SSH tunnel to the registry's port 5000 on a loopback address (docker treats 127.0.0.0/8 as an insecure registry); sparklina pulled it as localhost/<repo>@sha256:<digest> through a loopback forwarder, which is why its RepoDigest carries the localhost name.
build.contents: One Python source file edited; no compile, no new wheels, no vendored serving runtime.
build.self_check: The patch refuses a model_runner.py whose sha256 is not the base's and asserts each edit lands once; selfcheck_kpool_tail_slot_mapping.py re-imports the V2 model runner, asserts it binds KpoolTailSpec, and asserts the edited runner, the carried mtp.py, the stock block_table.py and the four MLA sources hash to their recorded values.

edits.what: from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (CircularBufferSpec, KVCacheConfig, ...) gains KpoolTailSpec

slot_mapping_enabled.append(not isinstance(layer_spec, CircularBufferSpec)) -> not isinstance(layer_spec, (CircularBufferSpec, KpoolTailSpec)); upstream spells the same decision KpoolTailSpec.uses_slot_mapping = False

qualification.model: /mnt/shared/tessera-runs/moe/glm53-4layer-a4-e2m1x2-q896-l2 (GLM-5.3-Flash 4-layer stub: KDA, MLA, KDA, MLA; A4 routed experts; no MTP layer)
qualification.dtype: Tessera A4 stub (TESSERA_E2M1_K2 routed experts at q256 896)
checks_passed: Dockerfile self-check on sparky, 2026-09-28: the runner binds KpoolTailSpec; the edited runner, the carried mtp.py, the stock block_table.py and the four MLA sources hash to the recorded values.

Kernel-level reproduction in the base image with the stub's block-table geometry (PrismaBuild action 1894e264, sparky): with the base rule the CUDA memcheck tool reports 98 invalid global reads in _compute_slot_mappings_kernel at block_table.py:344, all in program (1,0,0) (the kpool-tail group), the first at 0x420 bytes past the tail table's start, i.e. flat entry 264 = position 1056, past the 1 KiB table and the 32-byte allocation after it; with the tail opted out, 0 errors. Both rules write the same tail slots, 7*4 + position % 4, because the kpool-tail builder overwrites the generic row.

Serve-level memcheck pair on sparky, 2026-09-28 (eager, PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 so the tail table is its own allocation, compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --padding 8192 on _compute_slot_mappings_kernel, one 3649-token prompt): the base image reports 128 invalid 4-byte reads at block_table.py:344, all in program (1,0,0), 129 to 253 bytes past the 1 KiB tail table, and the engine core dies with 'unspecified launch failure'; this image reports 0 access errors and the prompt completes (arms memSn4 and memNn4). With the caching allocator on, the base image also reports 0 (memSn3): the overrun stays inside the allocator's segment, which is why eager serves of the base image have not faulted.

CUDA-graph serves on this image, FULL_DECODE_ONLY: 19 two-chunk 3649-token prefills (2048 + 1601 tokens) across four serves with no illegal memory access (fdoN8 10, fdoN2 4, fdoN1 3, fdoNmc3 2; fdoP1 5 more); fdoNmc3 ran under memcheck with 0 access errors.

Equality suite on this image (48 greedy completions with the top 20 logprobs, batches admitted paused): with every capture size 1 to 8, FULL_DECODE_ONLY (fdoN8 pass 2, digFN8), PIECEWISE (pwN2) and FULL_AND_PIECEWISE (fapN8, both passes) returned only outcomes that eager serves of this image also returned; fdoN8 pass 1 has one completion outside them whose difference starts in a prefill that ran eagerly.
Tessera's GLM53 NoPE gate tests inside this image: 68 passed, 0 skipped (PrismaBuild action 14cf4228, Tessera commit 64a8ff8298, tessera PR #699).
not_qualified: Stub only: the 45-layer body, TP2 and the MTP drafter are not measured on this image.

The drafter path (speculator, positions=None) now leaves the tail row at the pad slot, as upstream does; before the backport it wrote at the generic row's out-of-bounds slots. Drafter acceptance on this image is not measured.

vLLM's default (padded) capture sizes run another reduction order: vLLM's mHC TileLang op picks its split-K by token count, and a batch of 5 replayed in the 8-token graph moved top-20 logprobs by up to 0.98081 nats. A padded configuration's quality is not measured; only every size from 1 to the largest captured returns eager's outcomes.
Requests above 2048 tokens are not repeat-exact in any mode (stock top-k arrival order, sampler.cu:267); the equality results cover requests of at most 2048 tokens.
